subtype: Splitting a project into checkable pieces [Response]
passage: I'm Vandana, and I share a lab table with Tarun. On Monday I noticed Tarun staring at the fifty-page project report, shoulders low. Then Tarun took a pack of index cards and wrote one job on each: “collect data table,” “write the method,” “draw figure 1,” and so on until there were nine, each labelled with a time of under an hour. A phone timer sat beside the cards. After each job Tarun crossed a card off and stacked it on the right. By four, five cards were in that pile, and Tarun looked lighter, humming a little. I couldn't tell for certain what Tarun felt, only that the shoulders had come up.

qa.q: How many cards did Tarun write jobs on?
qa.a: Tarun wrote jobs on nine cards, each labelled with a time of under an hour.

qa.q: What might Tarun have felt by four o'clock?
qa.a: Tarun probably felt lighter and calmer, since the humming and the raised shoulders suggest the dread had eased, though Vandana cannot be sure.

qa.q: What did the card pile give Tarun as the day went on?
qa.a: Every finished card gave real proof of progress, so the report felt smaller and less scary.

qa.q: How does Vandana interpret Tarun's shoulders?
qa.a: Vandana treats the low shoulders as a sign of heaviness at the start and the raised shoulders as relief, but admits only guessing.

grounding: A wise worker divides a large task into pieces under an hour and ticks them off, seen by an observer.

passage:
Day 1, Sunday. The thirty-slide seminar felt like a mountain, and Hrithik sat in the hostel room with the laptop shut and his stomach tight. He tore a page from a notebook and wrote ten pieces, each one doable in under an hour: outline, slides 1 to 3, one chart, and so on. He ticked “outline” before dinner.

Day 3, Wednesday. Rukmini from his project group called to check in. Six ticks were done. “Feels weirdly light,” Hrithik said.

Day 6, Saturday. The tenth tick went in on a full page of ticks. He practised the talk once aloud and slept easily.

qa.q: How many pieces did Hrithik write on the page?
qa.a: Hrithik wrote ten pieces, each doable in under an hour.

qa.q: Why was Hrithik's stomach tight on the first day?
qa.a: Hrithik was dreading the thirty-slide seminar because the whole job looked huge and he could not see how to finish it.

qa.q: What effect did the ticks have between Sunday and Saturday?
qa.a: Each tick gave Hrithik real evidence of progress, so the dread shrank from a mountain to a page of finished pieces.

qa.q: What might Rukmini think when Hrithik says it feels weirdly light?
qa.a: Rukmini probably feels relieved and glad that Hrithik is on track, since Rukmini called to check in on the group work.

grounding: A wise worker splits a large task into checkable pieces, and each completed piece lowers dread over several days.
